messages:
Hannah: Heads up 9999UTC: p99 tail is climbing in usw1. Telemetry points to a tenant 'image-bulk' doing parallel warmups across racks. NIC TX queues and kvcache regen correlation high. Anyone able to triage?

Diego: I'm on. saw ~8 hosts with sustained egress bursts and kvcache_evictions jumped. This is more of a warmup storm than pure inference load.

Mei: If it's warmups, carving risks heavier rebalance churn. Quick mitigations: 1) egress policer + nic shaping, 2) short dedicated micro-slice (1-2 GPUs) with strict egress and kvcache pin, 3) route their staging traffic to a heavily-throttled preemptible pool. I lean to 1 then escalate.

Hannah: Agree 1 first. Diego, can you identify top-3 offending hosts and apply nic-shaper? Also apply tenant-level egress cap 100mbps soft-quarantine for 2h.

Diego: Running commands now:

```
rwdctl host patch --hosts h12,h13,h14 --nic-shaper tx=180mbps
rwdctl tenant update image-bulk --egress-limit 100mbps --soft-quarantine true --quarantine-ttl 2h --fallback preemptible
```

ops-bot: Created incident INF-5109: "image-bulk warmup -> egress cap + nic shaping". Runbook https://redwood.internal/runbooks/noisy-warmup

Rafael: One (non-blocking) ask: can we auto-detect repeat offenders and surface a "burst-window" opt-in? tenants that repeatedly trigger soft-quarantine get invited to prepay or schedule short reserved windows. Would avoid repeated manual ops.

Mei: +1. Also a technical add: allow kvcache pre-warm handshake in the API so when a tenant requests a burst-window we can prefill shared warm slots or pin small shards to reduce regen storm.

Hannah: For now keep the policer for 2h and monitor. If p99 improves, drain over 20m. Diego, post telemetry back in 10m. Rafael, let's sync on a short RFC for burst-windows (API + pricing + fast carve flow).

Diego: Initial: p99 down ~19%, host nic tx down ~50% on patched hosts, kvcache_evictions down ~42%. A small % (~5%) of requests hit the preemptible fallback. Will report at +10m.

Rafael: Nice. For the RFC I'll sketch: burst-window types (on-demand vs scheduled), pricing model (per GPU-hour + egress premium), max duration, and a fast carve API with pre-warm handshake. Will ping product.

Hannah: Thanks. Adding a runbook note: require customers to request burst-windows for large parallel warmups; infra can auto-enforce after 3 soft-quarantine events in 7d.

ops-bot: INF-5109 updated: assignees Diego (monitoring), Rafael (RFC), Mei (pre-warm API sketch).
